newsitem.title: DENMARK: Berendsen says one-off costs hit earnings.
newsitem.headline: Berendsen says one-off costs hit earnings.

text.p: Denmark's Sophus Berendsen said on Monday that losses in its Electronics and Data division and one-off costs would cut 1996 results before associated company earnings and tax to 145 million crowns ($25.1 million) from 1995's 275 million.
The electronics division would swing from profit of 40 million crowns in 1995 to an expected loss of around the same amount in 1996, Managing Director Hans Werdelin told Reuters.

"In connection with that there are one-off costs for closing of unprofitable product lines, adjustment of inventory and redundacy payments," he said, adding that divisional chief Niels Hjertholm had been replaced.
"One-off costs resulting from the decisions taken give the effect that we now see," Werdelin said. He would not say if he was considering selling the division.

The forecast excludes part-owned earners such as Rentokil, the British security to pest control firm which contributed 533 million crowns pre-tax to Berendsen's first-half group result of 640 million crowns.
Rentokil, 37.5 percent owned by the Danish company, nevertheless saw its share buffeted on the London Stock Exchange, while in Copenhagen Berendsen stock plunged seven percent to close at 675 crowns.
Werdelin said that Hjertholm had been over-optimistic in his projections for the division under harsh conditions.

"When you have prices falling by up to 90 percent and at the same time the market turns against you, you can see how much more you have to sell to stay covered and that much we couldn't sell," he said. ($ = 5.782 Danish Crowns)
